1.1.31 — Press to peek

  • Force click a link to see it in a preview that grows out of where you pressed. Shift-click still works too.
  • Site settings. The slider button in the address opens a glass panel for the site you're on: whether it's secure, switches for sound, ad blocking, pop-out video and separate logins, its zoom, and its cookies.
  • A tidier sidebar. The space's name sits under the address, your initials sit at the bottom, and hovering a tab is instant.
  • A new welcome. Meet Pane fills the window, follows light and dark, brings your tabs over from Arc, Chrome, Dia, Helium and more, and shows how a new tab really works.
  • A new icon.

1.1.30 — Tidy menu

  • No more wrapped names. The glass menu at the bottom of the sidebar keeps every label on one line, and grows a little wider than a narrow sidebar when it needs to.

1.1.29 — Moves with you

  • Controls that step aside. With the sidebar showing, back, the address and reload float over the page in glass. Scroll down and they blur away, leaving just the site's name; scroll up and they're back. Page options › Move Controls to Sidebar puts them where they were.
  • A new New Tab page. See-through glass with one search box, a + for quick actions, dictation, and a Top Sites chip. New windows open on it too.
  • Liquid Glass search. The New Tab box and its suggestions are one sheet of glass that springs open beneath it.
  • Glass tabs. The tab you're on, the address field and pinned tiles are Liquid Glass pills.
  • More room. The sidebar sits further from the window's edge.
